The '''Detailed Surface Scanner''' ('''DSS''') is an optional internal module used to scan planets, moons, rings, and other bodies within a system, revealing surface detail, geological and biological signal counts, and other body-specific information used for exploration data value, site-hunting, and [[Mining|mining]] route planning.

== Overview ==

Firing Detailed Surface Scanner probes at a body reveals a fuller data set than the system-wide discovery scan alone provides, and is a prerequisite for locating many body-specific points of interest. It is distinct from [[Sensors]], the core internal module governing general contact detection range.

== Mining role ==

For mining, the DSS is used to map [[Planetary Rings|planetary rings]] and reveal [[Mining Hotspot|mining hotspots]]. A hotspot marker helps commanders choose where to enter a ring for [[Laser Mining|laser]], [[Core Mining|core]], or [[Sub-surface Mining|sub-surface]] runs.

A hotspot is only a targeting aid. After dropping into the ring, commanders still need to prospect individual asteroids, extract with the correct equipment, collect fragments or deposits, refine cargo, and verify current sell prices.
